full_judgment: 2. The opposite-party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 36 of 1985 in the 2nd Court of the Subordinate Judge, Comilla for specific performance of contract against the petitioners and opposite party Nos. 2-7 as the heirs of deceased Abdul Majid Mir alleging, inter alia, that Abdul Majid Mir while alive entered into a contract for sale of the suit-land with the plaintiff for a consideration of Taka 52,000.00 and executed a deed of agreement (bainapatra) on 23rd Kartick 1388 BS on receipt of Taka 30,000.00 as earnest money in presence of Abdur Rashid, Abdul Hoque, Abdul Kader and Siddiqur Rahman. Thereafter the said Abdul Majid Mir died leaving defendant Nos. 1-9 as his heirs and legal representatives who denied the contract as well as the receipt of any consideration money or giving delivery of possession of the suit tank. Thereupon the plaintiff instituted the said suit for specific performance of contract. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 the present petitioners only contested the suit by filing a written statement and denying all material allegations of the plaint and asserting that the bainapatra is a false, fraudulent and fabricated one and the alleged attesting witnesses did not see Abdul Majid Mir to execute the alleged Bainapatra. The plaintiff examined in all 6 PWs but none of the attesting witnesses and the contesting defendants examined only 3 DWs. The learned Subordinated Judge after hearing both the sides and on consideration of the evidence on record was pleased to dismiss the suit, holding, inter alia, that the alleged Bainapatra could not be proved by the plaintiff as genuine vide judgment and decree dated 30-5-91. Being aggrieved by the same the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.183 of 1991 in the Court of the District Judge Comilla which was transferred to the Court of the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Comilla for hearing and disposal. Then after observing all the formalities the appeal was made ready for hearing and the date was also fixed for the said purpose. But on 31-10-92, the plaintiff-appellant filed an application under Order 41, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure for taking the additional evidence of one Md. Siddiqur Rahman, son of late Azizullah of village Sreemontapur, Police Station Chandina, District Comilla along with some documents as the said witness was at Singapore and away from the country at the relevant time of trial of the suit, and further stating in the said application that during the pendency of the suit out of the 4 attesting witnesses of the Bainapatra, witnesses Abdur Rashid and Abdul Hoque were gained over by the contesting defendants and, as such, they refused to depose in favour of the plaintiff and that Abdul Kader, another attesting witness, was suffering from serious illness who ultimately died and could not come to depose and that Md. Siddiqur Rahman, another attesting witness, was away from the country and, as such, he could not be produced before the court as witness in due course but now he has returned home and staying in the country, hence in the interest of justice his evidence should be taken as additional evidence in the appeal under Order 41 rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure and some documents namely, a Barga Kabuliat dated 1-10-89 executed by defendant No. 2 Mosharraf Hossain and also First Information Report , charge-sheet and a compromise petition and order sheet of case No. 68/89 of Thana Magistrate, Debidwar should be admitted into evidence. Copy of the said application was received by the defendant-respondents with objection and the application under Order 41 rule 27 CPC came up for hearing in the court of the learned Additional District Judge on 20-1-93.
